Estrogen action on the liver leads to increased secretion of cortisol and growth hormone binding proteins, thus reducing the anabolic actions of GH, which are essential for mood stability, especially in women of reproductive and postnatal age.

the incidence of depression in females is linked to estrogen dependent increased secretion of various hormone-binding proteins.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased incidence of depressive disorders in women can be explained by a mechanism that includes the action of estrogen on the liver to enhance secretion of various hormone-binding proteins.
the incidence of depression can be linked to estrogen-dependent secretion of transcortin and other hormone binding proteins.
the increased incidence of mood disorders in women can be related to the increased levels of estrogen binding proteins, that in turn lead to increased cortisol levels and reduced GH exposure.
